chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who looks at the beauties of a woman whom he intends to marry, he said: 'There is no harm; he is merely observing. If a matter becomes decided/established, it will be so.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to look at a woman's face and body before marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of a man viewing a potential bride's physical features to ensure compatibility, a practice rooted in the Prophet's tradition of looking at the woman before marriage. The term 'istimam' (glancing) indicates a casual, non-lustful observation that does not incur sin, provided it serves the legitimate purpose of marriage selection. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between permissible pre-marital inspection and prohibited lingering gazes.
